regions.name: Central Sahel
regions.why: A semi-arid belt that lived a great drought in the 1970s–80s.

regions.name: Central Cameroon
regions.why: From the equatorial forest to the savanna.

PRECTOTCORR.label: Precipitation
PRECTOTCORR.simple: How much rain and snow falls, in millimetres of water per day (1 mm on one square metre is one litre). MERRA-2 corrects its model rain with rain gauges and satellite observations.

GWETROOT.label: Root-zone soil wetness
GWETROOT.simple: How wet the soil is where plant roots drink (roughly the top metre): 0 % is bone dry, 100 % is completely soaked.

T2M.label: Air temperature
T2M.simple: How warm the air is 2 metres above the ground — what a thermometer in the shade shows.

SLP.label: Sea-level pressure
SLP.simple: The weight of the air above a spot, as if measured at sea level (about 1013 hPa on average): low pressure brings storms, high pressure fair weather.

metas.text: Root-zone soil wetness (Central Cameroon) & Air temperature (Central Cameroon): the same months push these dynamics out of their norm (or back into it) together far more often than chance (meta molette born 2016-02, degrees 1, 2, 3), in opposite directions 80 % of the time.

Sea-level pressure (Central Cameroon) & Sea-level pressure (Central Sahel): the same months push these dynamics out of their norm (or back into it) together far more often than chance (meta molette born 2009-02, degrees 1, 2, 3), in the same direction 97 % of the time.

links.text: Sea-level pressure (Central Sahel) and Sea-level pressure (Central Cameroon) leave their norm in the same months, the same way: 62 times, where chance at the same moment of the record would give 19 (p = 5e-20; z = 14.0 against the same reading with one of them moved 1 to 5 years, beyond the shared trend and the persistence of each).
links.model_note: both series come from the MERRA-2 reanalysis, not from two independent instruments: confirm it with an independent dataset before calling it a finding

story.text: Opposite trends: precipitation is rising in Central Sahel and falling in Central Cameroon. One process can push the same variable in opposite directions in two places — look at the links below to see whether the same months move both.

Opposite trends: root-zone soil wetness is rising in Central Sahel and falling in Central Cameroon. One process can push the same variable in opposite directions in two places — look at the links below to see whether the same months move both.

Root-zone soil wetness — Central Sahel: +0.62 % per decade (95 % range +0.406 to +0.88). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 3.5e-07, t-test p = 2.5e-06. Eva: Since 2011, 81 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Air temperature — Central Cameroon: +0.37 °C per decade (95 % range +0.236 to +0.55). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 0.00024, t-test p = 0.0092. Eva: Since 2011, 71 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

story.text: Precipitation — Central Sahel: +0.09 mm/day per decade (95 % range +0.0508 to +0.135). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 9e-05, t-test p = 2.5e-05. Eva: Since 2011, months come out above Eva's expectation 57 % of the time: not clearly different from her 1981–2010 norm.

Air temperature — Central Sahel: +0.14 °C per decade (95 % range +0.0329 to +0.262). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 0.013, t-test p = 0.0041. Eva: Since 2011, months come out above Eva's expectation 53 % of the time: not clearly different from her 1981–2010 norm.

Sea-level pressure — Central Sahel: +0.07 hPa per decade (95 % range +0.00292 to +0.158). A rising trend that only one test (or only the 90 % level) supports. Mann-Kendall p = 0.039, t-test p = 0.098. With this much natural variability, a trend of this size needs about 67 years of data to stand out (45 so far). Eva: Since 2011, 70 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Precipitation — Central Cameroon: -0.20 mm/day per decade (95 % range -0.375 to +0.0169). A falling trend that only one test (or only the 90 % level) supports. Mann-Kendall p = 0.071, t-test p = 0.077. With this much natural variability, a trend of this size needs about 48 years of data to stand out (45 so far). Eva: Since 2011, 58 % of months came out lower than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Root-zone soil wetness — Central Cameroon: -2.4 % per decade (95 % range -4.33 to -0.356). A falling trend that only one test (or only the 90 % level) supports. Mann-Kendall p = 0.025, t-test p = 0.052. With this much natural variability, a trend of this size needs about 48 years of data to stand out (45 so far). Eva: Since 2011, 64 % of months came out lower than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Sea-level pressure — Central Cameroon: -0.008 hPa per decade (95 % range -0.211 to +0.159). A falling tendency that is not significant (yet): it could be chance. Mann-Kendall p = 0.91, t-test p = 0.97. With this much natural variability, a trend of this size needs about 242 years of data to stand out (45 so far). Eva: Since 2011, 65 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.
